subject: Literature
subcategory: The Art of the Short Story
title: The Arabian Nights and Frame Narratives
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Arabian Nights and Frame Narratives.

hook.text: A queen saves her own life by telling a story every night so captivating the king spares her until morning.

buildup.text: Scheherazade tells a thousand and one tales, nesting stories within stories in an intricate frame narrative.

discovery.text: The collection blends Persian, Arab, Indian, and Egyptian tales accumulated over many centuries and cultures.

twist.text: Aladdin and Ali Baba, the most famous stories, were not in the original text but were added by a French translator.

climax.text: The Arabian Nights invented the frame narrative, where storytelling itself becomes the engine of the plot.

punchline.text: The greatest stories were told to postpone death.

quiz.question: What surprising fact about Aladdin and Ali Baba is true?
options: They were the oldest stories in the collection
They were not in the original text but added by a French translator
They were written by Scheherazade herself
